newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends higher on firm cash prices.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends higher on firm cash prices.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled higher Wednesday, taking their strength from cash prices in the southwestern U.S.
"The market seems overly short for April, May and June," said one East electricity broker, attributing to shortcovering helping the day's rise.
"It was one player that came in and bought it up," argued one Houston futures trader.
May California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled 23 cents at $10.40 a megawatt hour (MWh) after bouncing between $10.30 and $10.60.
June COB finished up seven cents at $10.75 while deferred COB months ended flat to 15 cents higher.

May Palo Verde (PV) settled up 32 cents at $14.87 after posting a high of $15.20. June PV finished up 29 cents at $15.75, near the day's high of $15.80. Other active PV contracts ended flat to 20 cents higher.

Day-ahead electricity prices for firm, peak delivery at the COB held steady at $11.00-12.00, while those at PV were at $14.50-15.25 on air-conditioning demand in parts of the Southwest and several regional power units remaining off line.
Southern California Edison said restart of the 1,070 MW unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear power plant has been delayed by another week to April 1.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear plant in Washington will be shut Thursday, several weeks earlier than planned for maintenance due to ample hydropower in the region.
There was also talk of an outage at the 750 MW unit 2 at the Navajo coal-fire plant in Arizona lasting as long as two weeks although the unit's status could not be confirmed.

In other Western news, capacity on the Pacific Intertie power transmission system, which links the Northwest to Southern California, will be raised to 6,250 megawatts (MW) by this weekend, a spokesman for Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said Wednesday.
BPA says it will be able to raise the Intertie capacity even without re-energizing the 500 KV John Day-Slatt line, although repairs to the line are also expected to be finished by Saturday.
Some market sources said fundamental factors do not support a substantial rise in the complex due to mild spring weather and plentiful hydroelectric supply.
In the Northwest, temperatures would average near normal along the coast and about 10 degrees Fahrenheit above normal in the extreme eastern area for the next several days.
In the Southwest, readings would run as much as nine degrees above normal in the northeast, but two to six degrees above normal through the rest of the region.
NYMEX estimated 169 COB and 538 PV contracts were sold, compared with 467 COB and 347 PV lots Tuesday.
